Why a data viewer

Print statements versus a data viewer

Print statements

The robot loop runs 50 times a second, so lines fly past.

You see one number at a time, with no shape to it.

Two values are hard to match up at the same moment.

A data viewer

Every value becomes a line you can read at a glance.

Everything shares one clock, so causes line up with effects.

You can pause, zoom in, and look again after the match.

Getting connected

Starting AdvantageScope and connecting to a robot

1

Open it

In WPILib VS Code: Ctrl+Shift+P, then WPILib: Start Tool, then AdvantageScope.

2

Set your robot address once

App > Show Preferences... > Robot Address. Team 1212 is 10.12.12.2.

3

Connect

File > Connect to Robot > Default: NetworkTables 4, or press Ctrl+K.

4

Watch the window title

It says Searching until the robot answers.

5

On a USB cable?

File > Use USB roboRIO Address switches to 172.22.11.2.

Level 1: see it live

Publishing a value with SmartDashboard

CANDriveSubsystem.java

@Override

public void periodic() {

  // Runs every 20 ms, even while the robot is disabled.

  SmartDashboard.putNumber("Drive/LeftAppliedOutput", leftLeader.getAppliedOutput());

  SmartDashboard.putNumber("Drive/RightAppliedOutput", rightLeader.getAppliedOutput());

  SmartDashboard.putNumber("Drive/BatteryVolts", RobotController.getBatteryVoltage());

}

The key becomes a field. In the sidebar, open SmartDashboard, then Drive.

6

Level 2: save it to a file

Saving a log with DataLogManager

Robot.java

public Robot() {

  // Save every NetworkTables change to a .wpilog file.

  DataLogManager.start();

 

  // Also record the enabled state and the joysticks.

  DriverStation.startDataLog(DataLogManager.getLog());

 

  // Level 3, next slide: log every @Logged class.

  Epilogue.bind(this);

}

By default the robot saves nothing. These two lines change that. The last line is next.

Level 3: the 2026 best practice

Logging whole classes with Epilogue

CANDriveSubsystem.java

1 @Logged

  public class CANDriveSubsystem extends SubsystemBase {

2   // Robot() calls Epilogue.bind(this), which reads these.

3   public double getLeftCurrentAmps() {

      return leftLeader.getOutputCurrent();

    }

   

3   public double getRightCurrentAmps() {

      return rightLeader.getOutputCurrent();

    }

   

4   @Logged(name = "BrownedOut")

    public boolean isBrownedOut() {

      return RobotController.isBrownedOut();

    }

1

Tag the class

Tag Robot and RobotContainer too.

2

One line starts it

Epilogue.bind(this), from the last slide.

3

Public, no arguments

These methods are logged for you, and so are fields.

4

Pick a name

name sets what you will see in the log.

Logs

Getting a log off the robot

1

Best: a USB stick in the roboRIO

FAT32, in place before code starts. Logs go in a logs folder on the stick.

2

No stick?

Logs go to /home/lvuser/logs. WPILib warns against this on a roboRIO 1.

3

Copy it

Pull the stick with the robot off, or use File > Download Logs....

4

Check the folder

Robot Log Path starts as /U/logs, the stick. Change it for internal storage.

5

Open it

File > Open Log(s).... REV .revlog and CTRE .hoot files open the same way.

Log Files docs

docs.advantagescope.org

10

Best practice

What to log and how to name it

Log inputs and outputs, put units in the names, and log more than you think you need.

You cannot record something after the match is over. Inputs are what the robot sensed. Outputs are what it asked for. With both, you can tell whether the code or the machine went wrong.

Drive/Left             // Left what? How big?

Drive/LeftCurrentAmps  // Clear, and AdvantageScope labels the axis

Common mistake

When nothing shows up live

What you seeWhy it happensThe fix
Title stuck on SearchingWrong Robot Address. A new install starts at 10.00.00.2.Set 10.TE.AM.2 with your own team number.
Searching, on a USB cableThe USB address is not the radio address.File > Use USB roboRIO Address.
Searching, or an empty sidebarWrong mode: Connect to Simulator, or the AdvantageKit, Phoenix or RLOG source.File > Connect to Robot > Default: NetworkTables 4.
Connected, but your field is missingThe code never published it, or was never deployed.Add the put to periodic() and deploy again.

12

Common mistake

The log is empty or missing

What you see

Failed to open log folder or No files found in folder, or a file with almost nothing in it.

Why it happens

Logging never started, no Driver Station was connected, or Robot Log Path is the wrong folder.

The fix

Call DataLogManager.start(), connect the Driver Station, and match the path to where logs really are.

14

Exercise

Graphing left and right applied output

1.

Copy periodic() from Level 1 into your CANDriveSubsystem, add the imports, and deploy.

2.

Put the robot on blocks, wheels off the floor. No robot? getAppliedOutput() reads 0 in the simulator, so run Level 3 and graph Left Motor Speed under Robot/container/drive/drive.

3.

Connect AdvantageScope, then open SmartDashboard and Drive in the sidebar.

4.

Drag LeftAppliedOutput and RightAppliedOutput to Left Axis.

5.

Enable. Push the left stick forward, then use the right stick to turn.

Done when: both lines follow the sticks, and they move differently when you turn.
